meanings.note: Very common colloquial pronunciation/variant of すみません.

examples.text: すいません、ちょっと通してください。
examples.trans: Excuse me, please let me through.

meanings.note: Plain い-adjective describing either late timing or slow speed.

examples.text: 今日は帰りが遅いです。
この電車は少し遅いですね。
examples.trans: This train is a little slow, isn't it?

meanings.note: Expresses change of state, or in polite customer service (になります) states an arrangement or price total.

examples.trans: That comes to one thousand yen.

meanings.note: Ichidan verb; causative 食べさせる can mean 'to feed/support'.

examples.text: 朝ごはんを食べましたか。
家族を食べさせるために働く。
examples.trans: I work to support my family.

meanings.note: Follows a verb's て-form or polite お + stem (お待ちください, お持ち帰りください) to make a polite request.

examples.text: ここに書いてください。

meanings.note: Special reading きょう.
Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.

meanings.en: whichever (after question word); or something like
meanings.note: After どれ (どれでも) means 'any one at all'; after a noun (店でも) suggests an example ('a shop or something').

examples.text: いつでも来てください。
お茶でも飲みませんか。
examples.trans: Won't you have tea or something?

meanings.note: Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).
Plain い-adjective.

examples.text: 彼の英語は本当にすごい。

原石.gloss: diamond in the rough, raw gem

meanings.en: diamond in the rough, raw gem

examples.text: 今日ね、街でものすごい原石を見つけたんですよ。
examples.trans: Today on the street, I spotted an incredible diamond in the rough.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.
Ichidan verb: blunt imperative 見ろ ('look!') is rough command speech.
All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.
Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.

examples.text: もう少し新人の発掘に力を入れませんか？
examples.trans: Why don't we put a bit more effort into discovering new talent?

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.
Godan verb: potential polite 入れます (はいれます) means 'can enter'.

examples.text: 予約なしでも入れますか。
examples.trans: Can we get in without a reservation?

meanings.note: Polite/dialectal negative ending, especially in ～ません.
Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.

meanings.en: that (near the listener or just mentioned)
meanings.note: Must always precede a noun (その椅子 'that chair').

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Can stand at the head of a sentence without a particle ('right now').
Godan intransitive verb; 黙ってろ! is a rough 'Shut up!'.
Marks the presence of a person (責任者はいるか) or follows て-form (often contracted to てる/てます in speech).
Replaces は, が, or を to add 'also' or 'too'.

examples.trans: Please give me this one too.

examples.text: あそこも新しい店です。
examples.trans: Over there is a new shop too.

examples.text: 今は黙っていても志願してくる子たちがいるんですよ。
examples.trans: Right now, girls volunteer on their own even without us scouting.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: come; go do something and return (after て-form)
meanings.note: Written in kana after a て-form (話してきます), expresses stepping away to do an action and coming back.

examples.text: ちょっと水を買ってきます。
examples.trans: I will go buy some water and be right back.

meanings.note: Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.note: Loanword from English 'series'.

examples.text: 新しいシリーズが始まります。

meanings.en: location of action; means; scope total
meanings.note: Marks where an action happens, the unit/scope of a rate or total (十日で, 全部で), or the cause/occasion.

examples.trans: It is one thousand yen in total.

meanings.note: Everyday spoken counterpart of なぜ or どうして.

examples.text: なんで知っているんですか。

meanings.note: Read なん before だ/です/の, and なに before が/を or alone.

examples.text: 何を買いにきましたか。
examples.trans: What did you come to buy?

meanings.note: Directly modifies a noun near the speaker (この店, この辺, この部分).

examples.text: この本は人気があります。
この前、芸能人がよく来るバーで飲んでたの。
examples.trans: The other night, I was having drinks at a bar where celebrities hang out.

examples.text: 芸能人とのエピソードを教えてくれた君に賞金をお贈りします。
examples.trans: We are offering prize money to callers who share celebrity stories.

meanings.note: Irregular verb: くる -> きます -> きました.

examples.text: この前、芸能人がよく来るバーで飲んでたの。
examples.trans: The other night, I was having drinks at a bar where celebrities hang out.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Covers everything from a casual chat to a business deal or idea.

examples.trans: Let us have a little talk.

meanings.en: do a favor for the speaker
meanings.note: After a te-form (会ってくれる？), warmly asks 'will you do that for us?'

examples.trans: Will you come again for me?

examples.text: 母が料理を作ってくれました。
examples.trans: My mother cooked food for me.

meanings.note: Loanword from English 'hotel'.

examples.trans: The hotel in front of the station.

meanings.en: go forward; work out well (いけます = 'it will work!')
meanings.note: Written in kana for figurative headway: いけます! ('this can go / this will work!'), 思いどおりにいかない ('does not go as hoped').

examples.text: この企画ならいけます！
examples.trans: With this plan, it will work!

examples.text: 仕事がうまくいっています。
お前ら、観光じゃないんだからしっかりしろよ。
examples.trans: Hey, this isn't sightseeing, so pull yourselves together.

examples.text: 彼女は来るんだろうな？
ちゃんとキャストはそろってるんだろうな？
examples.trans: You've got the whole cast properly lined up, right?

meanings.note: Connects a contrasting fact or trails off at the end of a sentence to voice a polite objection.

examples.text: お風呂に入りましたけど。
examples.trans: I already took a bath, though.

examples.text: 高いけど、おいしいです。

meanings.en: and so; because of that; with that

examples.text: それでどうなりましたか。
それで問題が解決しました。
examples.trans: With that, the problem was solved.

meanings.note: Refers to the upcoming occasion or a recent/current occasion.

examples.text: 今度一緒に食事しましょう。
examples.trans: Let's have a meal together next time.

meanings.note: Used in everyday farewells like またね, また明日, and また会いましょう.
